items.title: Constructed independent cell Gibbs states
items.design_state: Authored draft for the reserved A-page claim; hypotheses, caveats, and current supplier interfaces are recorded in batch-64 notes.
items.statement:
Let $r\ge1$ be finite. For each cell $i\in\{1,\ldots,r\}$, let $\mathcal H_i$ be a complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d_i\ge1$, let $H_i=H_i^*$ be a Hermitian proper Hamiltonian in joules, and let $Q_i=Q_i^*$ be a dimensionless number observable whose eigenvalues lie in $\mathbb N_0$. Assume $[H_i,Q_i]=0$. Operators $H_i,Q_i$ on the total space $\mathcal H:=\bigotimes_{i=1}^r\mathcal H_i$ mean their lifts acting on the $i$th tensor factor and as the identity on the other factors; no intercell interaction is included.

Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and let $O\subseteq M$ be a connected open set on which a smooth future-directed timelike Killing field $\xi$ is defined. Use length coordinates $x^0=ct$ and the corresponding dimensionless components of $\xi$. Define its dimensionless lapse $N(x):=\sqrt{-g_x(\xi_x,\xi_x)}>0$. Let $c>0$ be the speed of light in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $k_B>0$ Boltzmann's constant in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, and let $A$ be a global smooth real one-form with SI components in tesla-metres, $F:=dA$ with components in teslas, and $\Lambda_\xi:O\to\mathbb R$ a global smooth compensator in tesla-metres with $\mathcal L_\xi A=d\Lambda_\xi$. Define $\Phi_\xi(x):=-c\bigl((\iota_\xi A)_x-\Lambda_\xi(x)\bigr)$ in volts. Let $T:O\to(0,\infty)$ and $\mu:O\to\mathbb R$ be smooth fields in kelvins and joules per particle. Fix a common particle rest mass $m>0$ in kilograms and charge $q\in\mathbb R$ in coulombs, put $M:=mc^2>0$ in joules, and define $u:=\xi/N$, $\beta:=u/(k_BT)$ in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, and $\zeta:=\mu/(k_BT)$ dimensionlessly. On the future massive shell $\mathcal P_M^+(O):=\{(x,P)\in TO:g_x(P,P)=-M^2,\ P\text{ future-directed}\}$, where $P$ has energy-vector units and $g_x(P,P)$ has units $\mathrm{J^2}$, let $f(x,P):=\exp\bigl(\zeta(x)+g_x(\beta(x),P)\bigr)$, as defined for the same charged data in [[thm-tgr-electrochemical-stationarity]], and assume the exact whole-shell stationarity condition $\mathcal L_{F,q}f(x,P)=0$ for every $(x,P)\in\mathcal P_M^+(O)$, where $\mathcal L_{F,q}$ is the charged transport field in that supplier's formulation. This is the stationarity premise of [[thm-tgr-electrochemical-stationarity]]. Choose a cell-location map $\chi:\{1,\ldots,r\}\to O$ and set $x_i:=\chi(i)$. Define the lapse, compensated potential, proper temperature, and chemical potential at cell $i$ by evaluation:
$$N_i:=N(x_i),\qquad \Phi_i:=\Phi_\xi(x_i),\qquad T_i:=T(x_i),\qquad \mu_i:=\mu(x_i).$$
The same theorem supplies constants $T_K>0$ and $\mu_K\in\mathbb R$ such that
$$N_iT_i=T_K,\qquad N_i\mu_i+q\Phi_i=\mu_K,$$
where $q$ is the common particle charge in coulombs. This use of the charged smooth-geometry supplier retains its explicit $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ assumption.

Set $\beta_K=(k_BT_K)^{-1}>0$ in joules$^{-1}$, $\beta_i=N_i\beta_K=(k_BT_i)^{-1}$, $H_K=\sum_{i=1}^r(N_iH_i+q\Phi_iQ_i)$, and $Q=\sum_{i=1}^rQ_i$. Then the grand generator $G_K:=H_K-\mu_KQ$ is Hermitian and
$$G_K=\sum_{i=1}^rN_i(H_i-\mu_iQ_i).$$
The finite partition sums
$$Z_i:=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H_i}e^{-\beta_i(H_i-\mu_iQ_i)},\qquad Z:=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H}e^{-\beta_KG_K}$$
are positive and finite, with $Z=\prod_{i=1}^r Z_i$. The normalized Gibbs density factorizes exactly:
$$\rho:=Z^{-1}e^{-\beta_KG_K}=\bigotimes_{i=1}^r\rho_i,\qquad \rho_i:=Z_i^{-1}e^{-\beta_i(H_i-\mu_iQ_i)}.$$
It is a $\beta_K$-KMS state for the grand-generator dynamics on the full finite matrix algebra. On the neutral subalgebra $\mathcal A_0:=\{B\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H):[B,Q]=0\}$, grand-generator and physical $H_K$ dynamics coincide, so the restricted state is $\beta_K$-KMS for the physical dynamics there. This constructs only independent finite cells; it does not claim that an interacting system's reduced cell states are Gibbs states.

references.title: Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, §3.4, Definition 3.4.4 and finite Gibbs/KMS calculation, printed pp. 74, 76–77
David Ruelle, Topics in Quantum Statistical Mechanics and Operator Algebras, Chapter 1 §7 and Chapter 2 §6, printed pp. 13–14, 24

items.title: KMS orbit clock rescaling
items.design_state: Authored draft for the reserved A-page claim; hypotheses, caveats, and current supplier interfaces are recorded in batch-64 notes.
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a unital complex $C^*$-algebra and let $t\mapsto\alpha_t$ be a strongly continuous one-parameter group of $*$-automorphisms of $\mathcal A$. Let $\omega$ be a $\beta_K$-KMS state for $\alpha$ in the physical-time convention of [[def-qsm-kms-state]], where $\beta_K>0$ has units $\mathrm{J}^{-1}$ and $\hbar>0$ has units $\mathrm{J\,s}$. For a constant dimensionless $\lambda>0$, define
$$\alpha^\lambda_\tau:=\alpha_{\tau/\lambda},$$
where $t$ and $\tau$ are real time parameters in seconds. Then $\omega$ is a $\lambda\beta_K$-KMS state for $\alpha^\lambda$, with strip width $\lambda\beta_K\hbar$ seconds. Conversely, if $\omega$ is a $\widehat\beta$-KMS state for $\alpha^\lambda$, then it is a $(\widehat\beta/\lambda)$-KMS state for $\alpha$.

For the geometric interpretation, let $O$ be a connected open subset of a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g)$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and let $\xi$ be a smooth future-directed timelike Killing field on $O$ with dimensionless components in length coordinates $x^0=ct$, where $c>0$ is the speed of light in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Define $N_\xi(x):=\sqrt{-g_x(\xi_x,\xi_x)}>0$ and $u:=\xi/N_\xi$. For a selected point $x_0\in O$, let $I_K\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval in seconds containing $0$, and let $\gamma_{x_0}:I_K\to O$ be the $C^1$ integral curve of $c\xi$ with $\gamma_{x_0}(0)=x_0$, so $\gamma_{x_0}'(t_K)=c\,\xi_{\gamma_{x_0}(t_K)}$; this is the Killing orbit through $x_0$ with Killing-time parameter $t_K$. For a cell assigned to $x_i$, take $x_0=x_i$ and denote this curve by $\gamma_i$. Define its proper-time parameter from the metric by
$$\tau(t_K):=\frac1c\int_0^{t_K}\sqrt{-g_{\gamma_{x_0}(s)}\bigl(\gamma_{x_0}'(s),\gamma_{x_0}'(s)\bigr)}\,ds,\qquad \tau(0)=0.$$
By [[lem-tgr-killing-thermal-normalization]], $\xi(N_\xi)=0$, so $N:=N_\xi(x_0)>0$ is constant along this orbit. The metric definition then gives $d\tau=N\,dt_K$ and, with the chosen origins, $\tau=Nt_K$; equivalently $d\gamma_{x_0}/d\tau=cu$ for $u=\xi/N_\xi$. For $k_B>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ and reference temperature $T_K>0$ in kelvins, the inverse temperature $\beta_K=(k_BT_K)^{-1}$ rescales orbitwise to $\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}:=N\beta_K$; defining $T_{\mathrm{loc}}:=(k_B\beta_{\mathrm{loc}})^{-1}$ gives $T_{\mathrm{loc}}=T_K/N$. No spatially varying lapse is treated as one global time-rescaled automorphism group.

references.title: Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, §3.4, Definition 3.4.4, printed p. 74
David Ruelle, Topics in Quantum Statistical Mechanics and Operator Algebras, Chapter 1 §7, printed pp. 13–14

items.title: Finite response and spectral clock redshift
items.design_state: Authored draft for the reserved A-page claim; hypotheses, caveats, and current supplier interfaces are recorded in batch-64 notes.
items.statement:
Fix a cell label $i\in\{1,\ldots,r\}$ in [[thm-tgr-finite-cell-gibbs-factorization]], let $x_i=\chi(i)$ be its assigned point, and write $N:=N_i=N(x_i)>0$, $H_{\mathrm{loc}}:=H_i$, $Q:=Q_i$, and $\mu_{\mathrm{loc}}:=\mu_i$. Let $\beta_K>0$ in joules$^{-1}$ and $\mu_K$ in joules be the global parameters supplied there. Put $G_{\mathrm{loc}}:=H_{\mathrm{loc}}-\mu_{\mathrm{loc}}Q$ and $G_K:=NG_{\mathrm{loc}}$. Set $\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}:=N\beta_K$ and define the cell normalizer $Z_{\mathrm{loc}}:=Z_i=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H_i}e^{-\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}G_{\mathrm{loc}}}=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H_i}e^{-\beta_KG_K}>0$. Let $\sigma$ be the cell Gibbs density supplied by that theorem, so $\sigma=Z_{\mathrm{loc}}^{-1}e^{-\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}G_{\mathrm{loc}}}=Z_{\mathrm{loc}}^{-1}e^{-\beta_KG_K}$. For neutral Hermitian matrices, define
$$\alpha^{\mathrm{loc}}_\tau(C):=e^{iG_{\mathrm{loc}}\tau/\hbar}Ce^{-iG_{\mathrm{loc}}\tau/\hbar},\qquad \alpha^K_t(C):=e^{iG_Kt/\hbar}Ce^{-iG_Kt/\hbar}.$$
For this selected cell, let $q$ be the common charge in coulombs and $\Phi_i:=\Phi_\xi(x_i)$ its compensated potential in volts from the supplier. Define $H_{K,i}:=NH_{\mathrm{loc}}+q\Phi_iQ$ in joules, and write $H_K:=H_{K,i}$ in the physical control below. The supplier normalization gives $N\mu_{\mathrm{loc}}+q\Phi_i=\mu_K$, hence $H_K=G_K+\mu_KQ$.

Let $A=A^*$ and $B=B^*$ satisfy $[A,Q]=[B,Q]=0$. Then their local proper-time and Killing-time dynamics agree after $\tau=Nt$.

Let $h:[0,S]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, with $S>0$ seconds, and let $h(\tau)B$ have units joules. For dimensionless $\epsilon\in\mathbb R$, the proper-time grand-generator control $G_{\mathrm{loc}}-\epsilon h(\tau)B$ corresponds in Killing time to $G_K-\epsilon N h(Nt)B$. Define $E_{\mathrm{loc}}(\tau)$ and $E_K(t)$ as the finite-time expectations of $A$ from the same initial density $\sigma$ under these controls. Because $A$ and $B$ commute with $Q$, replacing each grand generator by its physical Hamiltonian changes the propagator only by a unitary generated by a constant multiple of $Q$ and leaves the expectation of $A$ unchanged. Thus these expectations also equal those obtained from the respective physical controls $H_{\mathrm{loc}}-\epsilon h(\tau)B$ and $H_K-\epsilon Nh(Nt)B$. In particular,
$$E_K(t)=E_{\mathrm{loc}}(Nt)\qquad(0\le t\le S/N).$$
The finite-time Kubo expansions have identical first-order terms under this rescaling and the same quadratic remainder bound. With
$$R_{\mathrm{loc}}(u):=\frac{i}{\hbar}\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\sigma[\alpha^{\mathrm{loc}}_u(A),B]\right),\qquad C_S:=\frac{2}{\hbar}\int_0^S|h(s)|\,\|B\|\,ds,$$
the local expansion is
$$E_{\mathrm{loc}}(\tau)=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma\alpha^{\mathrm{loc}}_\tau(A))+\epsilon\int_0^\tau h(s)R_{\mathrm{loc}}(\tau-s)\,ds+r_{\mathrm{loc}}(\tau),\qquad |r_{\mathrm{loc}}(\tau)|\le\|A\|\frac{(|\epsilon|C_S)^2e^{|\epsilon|C_S}}2.$$
Use $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds, so $C_S$ is dimensionless and $R_{\mathrm{loc}}$ has units $[A][B]/(\mathrm{J\,s})$. The Killing-time response kernel is $R_K(t)=R_{\mathrm{loc}}(Nt)$ and its control amplitude is $Nh(Nt)$.

For the equilibrium correlation spectral measures, use the Fourier convention of [[thm-qsm-dt-spectral-fdt]]. If $D_N(\omega):=N\omega$, then
$$S_K=(D_N)_*S_{\mathrm{loc}},\qquad S_K(\omega)=N^{-1}S_{\mathrm{loc}}(\omega/N)$$
in distribution notation; the measure form preserves the weights of delta-function spectral lines. Since $\beta_K\hbar(N\omega)=\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}\hbar\omega$, detailed balance is unchanged. Any zero-frequency atom remains an atom at zero and is not assigned a value by the coth formula, which remains restricted to nonzero frequencies.

For a static local perturbation $G_{\mathrm{loc}}-\lambda B$, where $\lambda B$ has units joules, the re-prepared Gibbs family satisfies
$$\left.\frac{d}{d\lambda}\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_\lambda B)\right|_{\lambda=0}=\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}\operatorname{Cov}_{\mathrm{KM},\sigma}(B,B)=N\beta_K\operatorname{Cov}_{\mathrm{KM},\sigma}(B,B)\ge0.$$
Here $\delta B:=B-\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma B)I$ and
$$\operatorname{Cov}_{\mathrm{KM},\sigma}(B,B):=\int_0^1\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\sigma^{1-u}\delta B\,\sigma^u\delta B\right)\,du.$$
It reduces to the ordinary variance when $B$ commutes with $G_{\mathrm{loc}}$; no such reduction is asserted otherwise. These are exact finite-dimensional deductions for the constructed neutral cell. They imply no infinite-time relaxation, dc transport coefficient, or response law for arbitrary interacting reduced states.

references.title: Ryogo Kubo, Statistical-Mechanical Theory of Irreversible Processes I, Journal of the Physical Society of Japan 12 (1957), section 2, printed pages 572–575
MIT OpenCourseWare 8.512, Theory of Solids II, Lecture 1: Linear Response Theory, sections 1.1–1.5

items.title: Completeness of countable square-summable sequences
items.design_state: Local mathematical supplier added under the Step 1 prerequisite rule; complete coordinate-limit proof is on the A page.
items.statement:
With the inner product and norm of [[def-square-summable-family-on-an-arbitrary-index-set]], the complex sequence space
$$\ell^2(\mathbb N_0,\mathbb C):=\left\{x=(x_n)_{n\ge0}:\sum_{n\ge0}|x_n|^2<\infty\right\}$$
is complete. Hence it is a complex Hilbert space in the sense of [[def-hilbert-space]].

references.title: Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, Chapter 2 §2.1, Definition 2.1.1 and Exercise 2.1.2, printed pp. 13–14 (PDF pp. 12–13)

items.title: Rotating mode Gibbs obstruction
items.design_state: Authored draft for the reserved A-page claim; hypotheses, caveats, and current supplier interfaces are recorded in batch-64 notes.
items.statement:
Let $\mathbb N_0=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$ and let $\mathcal H:=\ell^2(\mathbb N_0,\mathbb C)$ be the complex square-summable sequences with inner product $\langle x,y\rangle=\sum_{n\ge0}x_n\overline{y_n}$, linear in its first argument. Let $e_n$ be the sequence with value $1$ at $n$ and $0$ elsewhere. Write $\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ for the bounded complex-linear operators on $\mathcal H$, with operator norm $\|B\|:=\sup_{\|x\|_2\le1}\|Bx\|_2$; for $C\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$, $C^*$ is its bounded Hilbert-space adjoint, characterized by $\langle Cx,y\rangle=\langle x,C^*y\rangle$. A state on this operator algebra means a bounded complex-linear functional $\omega$ with $\omega(I)=1$ and $\omega(C^*C)\ge0$ for every $C\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$. Define the occupation-number operator
$$D(\mathcal N):=\left\{x\in\mathcal H:\sum_{n\ge0}n^2|x_n|^2<\infty\right\},\qquad (\mathcal Nx)_n:=nx_n.$$
For a densely defined operator $T$ on this space, use the adjoint relation
$$D(T^\dagger):=\left\{y\in\mathcal H:\exists z\in\mathcal H\ \forall x\in D(T),\ \langle Tx,y\rangle=\langle x,z\rangle\right\},\qquad T^\dagger y:=z.$$
The representing $z$ is unique when $D(T)$ is dense; here “self-adjoint” means $D(T^\dagger)=D(T)$ and $T^\dagger x=Tx$ on that domain.

Let $\epsilon>0$ be in joules, $m\in\mathbb Z$ a dimensionless azimuthal mode number, $\Omega\in\mathbb R$ an angular velocity in $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds, and $\beta_K>0$ in joules$^{-1}$. Set
$$H:=\epsilon\mathcal N,\qquad J:=\hbar m\mathcal N,\qquad a:=\epsilon-\hbar m\Omega.$$ 
For $m\ne0$, $J$ has domain $D(\mathcal N)$; for $m=0$, $J$ is the zero operator on all of $\mathcal H$. The operator $H$ has energy units J, $J$ has angular-momentum units J s, and $a$ has energy units J, so $\Omega J$ also has units J. Define $K_0:=H-\Omega J$ on the common domain $D(\mathcal N)$ and let $K:=\overline{K_0}$ be its operator closure. For $a\ne0$, $K=a\mathcal N$ has domain $D(\mathcal N)$; for $a=0$, $K$ is the zero operator on all of $\mathcal H$. Thus $K$ is the self-adjoint closure of the rotating generator $H-\Omega J$, including at the zero threshold. Then $\mathcal N$, $H$, $J$ and $K$ are self-adjoint on the stated domains.

Define the one-mode occupation partition sum by
$$Z_{\beta_K}(a):=\sum_{n=0}^\infty e^{-\beta_Kan}\in[0,+\infty].$$
It is the diagonal trace of the positive Gibbs weights in the occupation basis whenever the sum is finite. This sum is finite exactly when $a=\epsilon-\hbar m\Omega>0$, in which case
$$Z_{\beta_K}(a)=\frac{1}{1-e^{-\beta_Ka}}.$$
For $a>0$, the weights $p_n=Z_{\beta_K}(a)^{-1}e^{-\beta_Kan}$ sum to one and define the diagonal Gibbs functional
$$\omega_a(B):=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}p_n\langle Be_n,e_n\rangle,\qquad B\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H).$$
The proof shows that this is a state in the stated sense. For $a\le0$, the occupation partition sum diverges, so no normalized Gibbs state of this trace form exists. This is a single bosonic mode calculation; it constructs no continuum field state or rotating-spacetime equilibrium.

references.title: Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, §3.4, finite Gibbs/KMS calculation, printed pp. 76–77
David Ruelle, Topics in Quantum Statistical Mechanics and Operator Algebras, Chapter 1 §7, KMS and Gibbs-state discussion, printed pp. 13–14

title: Constructed independent cell Gibbs states — Examples

items.title: Proper clock two-level response
items.design_state: Authored exact finite-dimensional worked example under the reserved B-page scope; no apparatus or empirical claim.
items.statement:
Take a cell label $i$ from [[thm-tgr-finite-cell-gibbs-factorization]], with assigned location $x_i=\chi(i)$ and lapse $N:=N_i=N(x_i)>0$. For this neutral two-level example, take Hilbert space $\mathbb C^2$, number operator $Q=0$, and proper Hamiltonian
$$H_{\mathrm{loc}}=\frac{\Delta}{2}Z,\qquad \Delta>0\ \mathrm J.$$
Here
$$X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\quad Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\quad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$$
are dimensionless Hermitian Pauli matrices. Let $\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}=N\beta_K>0$ in joules$^{-1}$ and prepare
$$\sigma=\frac{e^{-\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}H_{\mathrm{loc}}}}{\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}H_{\mathrm{loc}}})}.$$
For the dimensionless observable and control $A=B=X$, the proper-time Kubo kernel, its Killing-time version, and the spectral measure are
$$R_{\mathrm{loc}}(\tau)=\frac{2}{\hbar}\tanh\!\left(\frac{\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}\Delta}{2}\right)\sin\!\left(\frac{\Delta\tau}{\hbar}\right),\qquad R_K(t)=\frac{2}{\hbar}\tanh\!\left(\frac{\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}\Delta}{2}\right)\sin\!\left(\frac{N\Delta t}{\hbar}\right),$$
$$S_{\mathrm{loc}}=2\pi\left(p_+\delta_{-\Delta/\hbar}+p_-\delta_{\Delta/\hbar}\right),\qquad p_+=\frac{e^{-\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}\Delta/2}}{2\cosh(\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}\Delta/2)},\quad p_-=\frac{e^{\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}\Delta/2}}{2\cosh(\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}\Delta/2)}.$$
The Killing-time spectral measure is the pushforward of $S_{\mathrm{loc}}$ under $\omega\mapsto N\omega$, so its two lines are at $\pm N\Delta/\hbar$ with the same respective weights. The oscillation period is $2\pi\hbar/\Delta$ in proper time and $2\pi\hbar/(N\Delta)$ in Killing time.

For the separately re-prepared static family
$$\sigma_\lambda:=\frac{e^{-\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}(H_{\mathrm{loc}}-\lambda X)}}{\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}(H_{\mathrm{loc}}-\lambda X)})},\qquad \lambda\ \mathrm J,$$
the static Gibbs susceptibility is
$$\left.\frac{d}{d\lambda}\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_\lambda X)\right|_{\lambda=0}=\frac{2}{\Delta}\tanh\!\left(\frac{\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}\Delta}{2}\right).$$
This finite model has persistent spectral lines and an oscillatory response. Its static Gibbs derivative is not a dc transport coefficient, and no infinite-time decay is asserted.

references.title: Ryogo Kubo, Statistical-Mechanical Theory of Irreversible Processes I, Journal of the Physical Society of Japan 12 (1957), §2, printed pp. 572–575
MIT OpenCourseWare 8.512, Theory of Solids II, Lecture 1: Linear Response Theory, §§1.1–1.5
